talking_points.headline: The agentic fault line opens: JPMorgan walls out outside AI agents while BofA, BBVA and Wells Fargo back the Sierra-Meta protocol
talking_points.context_html: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said the bank will not let outside AI agents into customer accounts, even as Bank of America, BBVA and Wells Fargo joined the Sierra-Meta Personal Agent Protocol to give agents verifiable credentials — while Jane Fraser, CEO of Citigroup, said AI benefits 'significantly outweigh' costs and Jeremy Barnum, CFO of JPMorgan, walked the bank's AI-spend estimate down from US$2bn. Agentic finance just split into two public strategies: walled gardens versus interoperable agents. For Adam, the fault line matters more than the winner — wealth programmes will soon have to pick a third-party-agent posture, and the industry's two answers are now on record.

talking_points.headline: The FSB writes the supervisory baseline for bank AI — agentic case studies included, human approval mandatory
talking_points.context_html: The Financial Stability Board's 'Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence', published 15 October, sets the global supervisory baseline with concrete agentic case studies: one bank's in-house fraud agent now authors ~75% of card-fraud rule updates with human approval of every rule, cutting fraud losses over 20%. It lands a day after US and European regulators' AI scrutiny we reported yesterday. For Adam, this is the checklist his programmes will be examined against — human-in-the-loop approval points, red-teaming and auditable agent behaviour are now baseline, and the case studies give him ready-made patterns to cite in design conversations.

talking_points.headline: HSBC's own voice enters the AI delivery debate: CIB CEO Roberts on implementation progress and quantum
talking_points.context_html: Michael Roberts, CEO of HSBC Corporate & Institutional Banking, told Bloomberg on 15 October about implementation progress on AI and quantum computing — the most senior HSBC delivery voice on AI this earnings week, as peers quantified AI returns and regulators circled. For Adam, the framing lands directly on his mandate: AI as an implementation story, with progress evidenced and controls in place — exactly the posture his change portfolio is expected to demonstrate as 2027 planning sharpens.

AI & Technology.title: JPMorgan bars outside AI agents from accounts as rivals join Sierra-Meta agent protocol
AI & Technology.summary: During earnings week Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said the bank will not allow outside AI agents to access customer accounts with client credentials ('We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in'), even as JPMorgan pushes its own Smart Cash money-movement tool. Bank of America, BBVA and Wells Fargo took the opposite side, joining the Personal Agent Protocol led by Sierra and Meta to give agents their own verifiable credentials. The same coverage has Jeremy Barnum, CFO of JPMorgan, revising the bank's AI-spend estimate down from US$2bn and Jane Fraser, CEO of Citigroup, saying AI benefits 'significantly outweigh' investment, citing Devin adoption to cut tech-vendor spend 30%. This is the first open strategic split on agentic finance: walled-garden agents versus interoperable credentialed agents. For Adam, the fault line matters more than the winner — client-facing agent strategies in his programmes will have to pick a posture on third-party agent access, and the industry's two answers just became public.

AI & Technology.title: Citi patents point to an AI wealth 'Avatar' that could reshape the advisor role
AI & Technology.summary: eFinancialCareers reports that newly published Citi patent filings reveal work on an AI 'Avatar' for wealth management — a digital agent able to carry elements of the client-advisor relationship, framed as potentially displacing or reshaping the traditional advisor role. The filings land amid a week of agentic-finance headlines from JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and the FSB. For Adam, Citi's patents are an early-warning signal on the wealth side of agentic AI: if a money-centre bank is staking claims on AI delivered advice, the RM role-design, client-coverage and adoption questions in his wealth programmes move from hypothetical to near-term roadmap items.

Regulatory & Markets.title: FSB issues sound practices for responsible bank AI, with agentic case studies
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The Financial Stability Board published 'Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence' on 15 October, its supervisory baseline for AI in financial services, including agentic-AI case studies: one large international bank built an in-house agentic fraud-detection system in three months that now authors about 75% of card-fraud rule updates — with human approval of every new rule — and cut fraud losses more than 20%; another regional bank red-teams agents by attempting to force unauthorised actions. The publication follows the US and European supervisory scrutiny of bank AI we reported yesterday. For Adam, the FSB document is the checklist his programmes will eventually be examined against: human-in-the-loop approval points, red-teaming discipline and auditable agent behaviour are now written into the global supervisory baseline, not best practice.

HSBC News.title: HSBC CIB chief Michael Roberts on the bank's AI and quantum computing progress
HSBC News.summary: Michael Roberts, CEO of HSBC Corporate & Institutional Banking, told Bloomberg on 15 October about implementation progress on AI and quantum computing at the bank, in a week when agentic-AI controls and AI returns dominated peer earnings commentary. The interview is the most senior HSBC voice on AI delivery since the group's wealth and payments units detailed their AI stacks. For Adam, the CIB CEO framing AI as an implementation story — not an experiment — is consistent with the posture his own change portfolio is expected to demonstrate: delivery progress, controls in place, value evidenced.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: RBC Wealth Management names Daniel Soo head of private banking, Singapore, in RM hiring push
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: RBC Wealth Management Asia appointed Daniel Soo, Managing Director and Head of Private Banking, Singapore — a veteran of UBS, Credit Suisse and Standard Chartered private banking — alongside seven relationship-manager hires and appointments across Singapore and Hong Kong drawn from Barclays, UBS, Julius Baer, J. Safra Sarasin, Citi and UOB private banking. The moves signal continued aggressive build-out of RBC's Asia PB franchise by a non-APAC player. For Adam, it is further evidence that senior RM talent in Singapore and Hong Kong is being actively repriced and poached — retention and capacity plans for his own RM population should assume this level of market aggression through 2027 planning.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Nomura International Wealth Management appoints Vijay Solomon MD in Singapore
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Nomura International Wealth Management has appointed Vijay Solomon, Managing Director in Singapore, as the Japanese private bank continues building its Southeast Asia franchise. The hire follows RBC's Singapore private-banking appointment announced a day earlier, marking a week of international wealth managers reinforcing senior Singapore coverage. For Adam, the back-to-back moves confirm Singapore private banking as an active talent and franchise battleground — the market where his platform and RM-efficiency investments will be most directly compared against new-entrant energy.
